entities.summary: Vitaly Ivanovich Churkin was a Russian diplomat. He served as Russia's Permanent Representative to the United Nations from 2006 until his death in 2017. Previously he was Ambassador-at-Large at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation (2003–2006), Ambassador to Canada (1998–2003), Ambassador to Belgium and Liaison Ambassador to NATO and WEU (1994–1998), Deputy Foreign Minister and Special Representative of the President of the Russian Federation to the talks on Former Yugoslavia (1992–1994), Director of the Information Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the USSR/Russian Federation (1990–1992).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As Russia's Permanent Representative to the United Nations from 2006 until his death in 2017, Vitaly Churkin played a key role in shaping international relations and responding to global crises such as the Syrian Civil War. His diplomatic efforts had significant regional impact on Eastern European politics.
